----Petitioner  Versus  State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent  Connected With  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 12583/2025  Rajender Teli S/o Late Shri Piyar Chand Teli, Aged About 43  Years, Resident Of Pur Police Station Pur District Bhilwara.

 ----Petitioner  Versus  State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Anirudh Krishan Choudhary for  Mr. Rakesh Matoria
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI CHIRANIA Order 06/11/2025 1.

The instant bail applications have been filed by the petitioners- Narayan Teli S/o Late Shri Piyar Chand Teli aged about 40 years and Rajender Teli S/o Late Shri Piyar Chand Teli aged about 43 years have been arrested by the police on 24.09.2025 in connection with FIR No. 14/2025 of Police Station - Pur, District - Bhilwara as registered by the police on 20.01.2025 in relation to an alleged private dispute regarding sale, purchase and transfer of
(Uploaded on 06/11/2025 at 06:05:40 PM)
[2025:RJ-JD:47697] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-12582/2025] their undivided property pertaining to an incident dated 28.06.2013, for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471 of IPC.

The petitioners' bail applications were rejected by the learned trial Court vide order dated 07.10.2025 and 08.10.2025 respectively, thereafter the petitioners have preferred this bail application under Section 483 B.N.S.S.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the accused-petitioners submits that the allegations as levelled are false and unfounded.
It is contended that the dispute is purely of personal civil dispute among family members regarding their inherited property.
The petitioners have no criminal antecedents of any serious nature.
The accused- petitioners are in custody and the trial of the case is likely to takelong time.
Therefore, the benefit of bail be granted to the accused-petitioners.

3. Learned Public Prosecutor strongly objected to the bail application and submitted that petitioner by committed forgery by preparing forged documents through which they sold the inherited property without obtaining the consent of the other persons who had an interest in the property,
therefore, the petitioners may not be granted bail.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
This Court noted that the offences alleged are triable by the Magistrate.
The petitioners have been in custody since 24.09.2025, and no further recovery is to be made from the present petitioners.
There is also a considerable delay of more than 12-13 years in lodging the impugned FIR against the petitioners.
The investigation is complete and the trial of the case may takes sufficiently long time.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances, this Court deems (Uploaded on 06/11/2025 at 06:05:40 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:47697] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-12582/2025] it just and proper to grant bail to the accused-petitioners under Section 483 B.N.S.S.
5.

Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 483 B.N.S.S. is allowed and it is directed that accused-petitioners - (1). Narayan Teli S/o Late Shri Piyar Chand Teli and (2).
Rajender Teli S/o Late Shri Piyar Chand Teli shall be released on bail in connection with FIR No.
14/2025 of Police Station - Pur, District -Bhilwara, provided they execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- each with two sound and solvent sureties of Rs.50,000/- to the satisfaction of learned trial Court for their appearance before that Court on each and every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till the completion of the trial.
The petitioners are further directed not to take undue advantage of liberty or misuse liberty.
It is made clear that the observation as made by this Court in the bail application will not affect the trial of the case.

6. It is made clear that in case the petitioners are found to be involved in any other offence after their release in the present matter, the learned Public Prosecutor shall be at liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail.

(RAVI CHIRANIA),J 156-157-KshamaD/-
